question.question: After damage, how are Larva, Adult and Queen death checked, when is a Carcass placed, and what if a Queen check draws a Retreat arrow?

fixed_key.expected_answer: Larva dies at 1 injury without Carcass. Adult draws one Attack card blood, dies if blood <= current injuries and leaves Carcass. Queen draws two, sums blood and compares same way; any Retreat arrow causes retreat via Event-card corridor number, discard Event, rather than normal numerical resolution.

standard: Correct means every requested material ruling is resolved, no contradictions/unresolved part; accept equivalent wording; key may contain unrequested context which is not automatically required. Do not borrow from other answers.

candidates.answer: 1) Add injury markers, compare current total: Larva dies at 1; Adult draws one blood card and dies if blood ≤ injuries; Queen draws two and dies if sum ≤ injuries. 2) Adult/Queen death places Carcass; Larva none. 3) Queen Retreat arrow substitutes retreat: draw Event and move via its corridor number.

1) Larva dies at 1 Injury; Egg is destroyed at 1 Injury. Creeper/Adult draw one Attack card and die if blood value is no greater than current total Injuries; Queen draws two and sums blood values, dying if the sum is no greater. 2) Adult/Creeper/Queen death removes miniature and places a Carcass in the Room; Larva leaves no Carcass. 3) Any Retreat arrow changes the check to retreat instead of numerical death; Queen retreats if either of its two cards has the arrow.

After adding Injury markers, check the Intruder’s Injury Effect using its current total Injuries. Larva dies at 1 Injury. Adult checks 1 Attack card’s blood value; blood value no greater than total Injuries kills it. Queen checks 2 cards and sums blood; sum no greater than Injuries kills. On death remove the miniature and place an Intruder Carcass in the Room for Adult and Queen (Larva has no Carcass). If any drawn Queen check card has Retreat arrow, retreat occurs instead of a numerical death result: move it via the Corridor number on a drawn Event card, then discard that Event card.

Larva and Egg die at 1 Injury. Creeper or Adult: draw one Intruder Attack card and compare blood value to total Injuries; blood less than or equal to Injuries means death. Queen: draw two cards and sum blood; sum less than or equal to total Injuries means death. A dead Creeper, Adult, Breeder or Queen leaves a Carcass in the Room; Larva does not. If any relevant injury-check card has a Retreat arrow, retreat replaces numerical death/endurance; for Queen, either of its two cards with arrow triggers retreat.

After damage, Larva (and Egg) dies at 1 Injury. Adult: draw 1 Intruder Attack card and compare its blood value to current injuries; it dies if blood is equal to or lower than injuries. Queen: draw 2 cards, add blood values, compare in the same way. A dead Adult or Queen leaves an Intruder Carcass in its Room (Carcasses for any dead Intruder except Larvae; the summary’s direct list also includes Creepers). If any Queen check card shows Retreat, it flees: draw an Event card and move it through the Corridor number in its movement section, then discard that Event card.

One Injury kills a Larva. Adult death is checked by drawing one Intruder Attack card and comparing its blood value to the Injury markers: blood equal to or lower than injuries means death. Queen death uses two cards and adds their blood values before comparison. A Carcass is placed for any dead Intruder except Larvae. If a Queen check draws a Retreat arrow, the Queen retreats; either of its two cards showing the symbol is enough, and it is moved through the Corridor indicated by a drawn Event card.

After damage, 1 Injury kills a Larva or Egg. For Creeper/Adult draw one Intruder Attack card and compare its blood value to current Injury markers; for Breeder/Queen draw two and add their blood values. If the blood value is equal to or lower than injuries, the Intruder dies. Place a Carcass for every dead Intruder except Larvae. If a death-check card shows a Retreat arrow, draw an Event card and move the Intruder along the Corridor number in its movement section; Queen/Breeders retreat if either card has the arrow.

A Larva or Egg dies from 1 Injury; remove its miniature and do not place a Carcass. For Creeper or Adult, draw one Intruder Attack card and kill it if the blood value is equal to or lower than its current injuries; place a Carcass. For Queen or Breeder, draw two and add the blood values, using the same comparison; place a Carcass if killed. During an Injury Effect check, a Retreat arrow makes the Intruder flee along the Corridor number on a drawn Event card; a Queen or Breeder retreats if either of its two cards has the arrow.

After placing Injury markers, a Larva dies at 1 Injury and is removed; no Carcass is placed for Larvae. An Adult is checked by drawing one Intruder Attack card: if its blood value is equal to or lower than its injury count, it dies and a Carcass is placed in the Room. A Queen is checked by drawing two cards, adding their blood values, and comparing the sum to its injuries; on death, a Carcass is placed. If a Queen check draws a Retreat arrow on either card, the Queen flees via a Corridor selected by an Event card. The summary does not specify a separate priority rule between a death result and retreat arrow on the same check.

One Injury kills a Larva (and an Egg). An Adult draws one Intruder Attack card and dies if its blood value is equal to or lower than its Injury markers. A Queen draws two cards, adds their blood values, and dies if the sum is equal to or lower than its Injury markers. Dead Intruders other than Larvae leave a Carcass token in the Room. If either card in the Queen's check has a Retreat arrow, the Queen retreats via a Corridor indicated by a drawn Event card instead.

One Injury kills a Larva. For an Adult, draw one Intruder Attack card and compare its blood number to the Injury markers: it dies if blood is equal to or lower than injuries. For a Queen, draw two cards and add their blood values, then compare the total the same way. A dead Adult or Queen leaves an Intruder Carcass token in the Room; Larvae do not leave Carcasses. If a Queen's check draws a Retreat arrow, retreat overrides the numeric death check: draw an Event card, move the Queen through the corridor numbered in its Intruder movement section, and discard that Event card; either of the Queen's two cards can trigger retreat.

A Larva dies at 1 Injury. A Queen is checked after damage by drawing 2 Intruder Attack cards and adding their blood values; if the total is equal to or below its Injury markers, it dies, and a dead Queen leaves a Carcass in the Room (Carcasses are placed for dead Intruders except Larvae). If either Queen card has a Retreat arrow, the Queen retreats instead of resolving a numerical endurance/death result: draw an Event card and move it through the Corridor number in its Intruder movement section, then discard that Event card. The summary does not specify what happens to the Queen's Injury markers if it survives the check.

1. A Larva dies from 1 Injury. 2. For an Adult, draw one Intruder Attack card: it dies if the blood value is equal to or below its current Injury markers. 3. For a Queen, draw two cards, add their blood values, and compare the total the same way. 4. A dead Adult or Queen leaves an Intruder Carcass token in the Room; Larvae are the exception and leave no Carcass. 5. If a Retreat arrow appears during an Injury Effect check, resolve retreat instead of the numeric death check; for a Queen, either of its two cards showing Retreat causes the retreat.

1) A Larva dies at 1 Injury. 2) For an Adult, draw 1 Intruder Attack card and compare its blood value to the Intruder’s Injury markers: blood equal to or lower than Injuries means it dies. 3) For a Queen, draw 2 cards, add their blood values, and compare the total to its Injury markers the same way. 4) A Carcass is placed for any dead Intruder except a Larva. 5) If any card drawn for the Queen’s Injury Effect shows the Retreat arrow, resolve retreat instead of a numerical death result: draw an Event card and move the Intruder through the Corridor given by its movement section, then discard that Event card.

After damage, 1 Injury kills a Larva (and an Egg). For a Queen, draw 2 Intruder Attack cards and add their blood values; it dies if the total is equal to or lower than its Injury markers. A Retreat arrow on either Queen check card replaces the numerical check: the Queen flees via the Corridor number on a drawn Event card. Place an Intruder Carcass in the Room for dead Intruders other than Larvae; the text does not state a Carcass for a dead Queen as an exception, so the general non-Larva rule applies.

After damage, place Injury markers on the Intruder and check its Injury Effect. A Larva dies at 1 Injury and is removed; an Adult is checked by drawing 1 Intruder Attack card and comparing its blood value to its injuries (blood value equal to or below injuries means death); a Queen is checked by drawing 2 cards and adding their blood values. On death, place an Intruder Carcass in the Room for any dead Intruder except a Larva (the Egg is likewise removed when killed at 1 Injury). If either card in a Queen’s check shows a Retreat arrow, it retreats instead of using a numerical death result: draw an Event card and move it through the Corridor number in that card’s Intruder movement section, then discard the Event card.

1. After Injury markers are added, check against the Intruder's current total injuries. A Larva dies at 1 Injury. 2. An Adult draws one Intruder Attack card for its blood value; blood less than or equal to its injuries kills it. 3. A Queen draws two cards and sums their blood values; a sum less than or equal to its injuries kills it. Adult and Queen deaths remove the miniature and place an Intruder Carcass in the Room; Larvae leave no Carcass. 4. If a Queen's injury check draws a Retreat arrow on either card, it retreats instead of resolving the numerical death check: draw an Event card and move it through the Corridor matching the card's Intruder movement number.

A Larva dies at 1 Injury; an Adult requires drawing one Intruder Attack card and dies if its blood value is no greater than its Injuries; a Queen requires drawing two cards and dies if their summed blood is no greater than its Injuries. 2. On a Queen's death, remove the miniature and place an Intruder Carcass in the Room. 3.
